name: Modern English
label: 4AD
lede: A Colchester art-school band that started out as the Lepers wrote a love song about the bomb dropping, and three years later it was closing out Valley Girl and giving 4AD its first American hit.

eras.title: The Lepers of Colchester
eras.text: Three friends in an Essex town started a band, put a single out on their own label and got picked up by 4AD. The first album sounded like a band that had listened hard to Joy Division.

years.src: Wikipedia: Modern English · The Big Takeover
years.h: Robbie Grey, Gary McDowell and Michael Conroy start the Lepers
years.p: In Colchester, Essex. Conroy, on bass, is 16 or 17. Before the year is out they've released a single on their own Limp label.
years.xp: They knew each other from Colchester pubs. "Nobody could play," Grey told the Big Takeover. "We just picked up instruments." Songs were built from what the band called "pieces," stuck together to see how they sounded.

years.h: Drums and keyboards arrive, and 4AD signs the band
years.p: Richard Brown and Stephen Walker make it a five-piece. [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]]'s 4AD signs them, and a John Peel session follows.

years.h: Mesh & Lace, produced by the band itself
years.p: Recorded at Jacobs Studios in Farnham with engineer Ken Thomas. Critics heard Joy Division all over it.
years.xp: Trouser Press's Ira Robbins called it "a load of monotonous droning and shouting by a precious art band oppressively weighed down by its self-conscious 4AD pretensions." The 2019 reissue's press release preferred "uncompromising experimentalists."

eras.title: A love song for the end of the world
eras.text: Hugh Jones took them to Rockfield and they came out with synths and a pop song. American radio found it as an import, a teen movie put it in front of millions, and the band moved to New York.

years.cap: Poster for the After the Snow tour, 1982
years.src: Spin · Trouser Press · Wikipedia: After the Snow
years.h: Hugh Jones and the band make After the Snow at Rockfield
years.p: Keyboards to the front. Sire's US release goes to No. 70 on the Billboard 200 and is certified gold.
years.xp:
Grey said they only learned verse and chorus from Jones, who "became another member of the band" for this record and the next. Trouser Press heard "a flawed but rewarding batch of hard-edged, melodic dance songs."

Other reviews were mixed. Nick Burton liked its "eccentric mix of genres and styles" but warned that the hit was "completely unrepresentative of the album."

q: We used to think 'God, we'll never make a pop record.'
years.src: Spin · The Big Takeover · Wikipedia: I Melt with You
years.h: Grey writes a love song about the bomb: 'I Melt with You'
years.p: A couple making love as the atomic bomb falls. In Britain it gets to No. 18 on the indie chart and misses the main one.
years.xp:
Grey says he wrote the words in about 20 minutes, sitting on the floor of his London house, stoned. "I could never write a straightforward love song," he told Spin. Jones told him to just talk into the microphone, which is why the verses sound half spoken.

Grey said it came out of an England of recession and nuclear fear. American stations started playing the import before anyone had promoted it there.

q: We used to play to 200 people in art college.
years.src: Wikipedia: I Melt with You · Spin
years.h: Valley Girl and MTV make 'I Melt with You' an American hit
years.p: The song plays in Martha Coolidge's teen film and goes into MTV rotation. It reaches No. 78 on the Hot 100 and No. 7 on the rock chart.
years.xp:
Next thing, Grey said, "we were in Daytona Beach playing to 5,000 people." The single went gold in the US and platinum in Canada.

The band only found out how much of the film it was in when they watched it: the song turns up twice. "The biggest country for us has always been America," Grey said in 2024. "We never understood why."

years.src: Wikipedia: This Mortal Coil · Wikipedia: Modern English
years.h: Ivo's idea for Modern English becomes This Mortal Coil
years.p: Watts-Russell wanted the band to record its live closer, a 'Sixteen Days' and 'Gathering Dust' medley. They said no, so he made it with them and [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]]' Liz Fraser and Robin Guthrie.
years.xp:
The result was the Sixteen Days/Gathering Dust EP, the first [[This Mortal Coil|60ef8ddb-7676-4056-a357-9a8c228d03a6]] release. Fraser and Guthrie's cover of Tim Buckley's 'Song to the Siren', meant as a B-side, became the A-side of the 7-inch and an underground hit.

Grey, McDowell and Conroy stayed involved with This Mortal Coil through 1984.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ricochet Days · Wikipedia: Modern English
years.h: Back at Rockfield for Ricochet Days
years.p: Hugh Jones produces again. It reaches No. 93 in the US, and the band relocates to New York.
years.xp: AllMusic's Alex Ogg found it "beautifully produced" but missed "the conviction and attack of old."

eras.title: Two splits and a second melt
eras.text: The five-piece came apart in New York. Grey kept the name going long enough to re-record the hit, then lost it to a label dispute.

years.cap: Modern English in a Sire Records press photo, c. 1986
years.h: Walker and Brown are gone by Stop Start
years.p: Aaron Davidson comes in on keyboards and guitar, with session drummer Graham Broad. It's the last album for Sire.
years.xp: Trouser Press said Stop Start "made it obvious which way Modern English was leaning, and it was nowhere particularly challenging."

years.h: Modern English breaks up
years.p: Eight years and four albums after the Lepers.

years.h: Grey re-records 'I Melt with You', and it charts again
years.p: Back together since 1989 with Conroy and Davidson, the band makes Pillow Lips for TVT. The new 'I Melt with You' reaches No. 76, two places higher than the original.
years.xp: The song kept paying. Grey told Louder it has "paid for everything we've ever done since," and the biggest single cheque was a Burger King advert in the early 1990s: $90,000. Walker, a vegetarian, had doubts before coming round.

years.h: Contract trouble with TVT ends the band again
years.p: Grey moves on to a new band, Engine.

eras.title: Engine turns back into Modern English
eras.text: When the TVT dispute was settled, Grey's new band took the old name. The records came slowly, with whoever was on the road with him.

years.h: Everything's Mad, on Imago
years.p: With the legal issues settled in 1995, Grey and keyboardist Matthew Shipley sign to Imago as Modern English.

years.h: Hugh Jones is back for Soundtrack
years.p: Songs built on US tours from 1998 to 2002 finally come out on Darla Records, with Jon Solomon on drums.

years.cap: Modern English playing 'I Melt with You' in Bend, Oregon
years.h: The original line-up, minus the drummer, reunites
years.p: Grey, McDowell, Conroy and Walker tour the US in July and September; the UK, Paris and the US follow in 2011.

eras.title: Still melting
eras.text: A film took the song's title, the band crowdfunded a record, and the band played network TV for the 40th anniversary of After the Snow.

years.h: Mark Pellington names a film I Melt with You
years.p: The director asks the band to re-record the song for it.

yt: 'I Melt with You' at Paste Studios, 2017
years.h: A PledgeMusic record produced by Martyn Young of MARRS
years.p: Take Me to the Trees is paid for by fans. The band also tours Mesh & Lace in the US.
years.xp: Young had made records as Colourbox for 4AD and was half of M/A/R/R/S, whose 'Pump Up the Volume' was 4AD's first UK No. 1.

years.h: Conroy plays bass at Lush's farewell show
years.p: [[Michael Conroy|b27d86eb-0879-44ae-98e3-6ac8a2569758]] fills in for [[Lush|697801d1-68b2-4413-a7e4-0ef507d21cc1]] at Manchester Academy, then joins Miki Berenyi in Piroshka in 2018.

years.cap: Robbie Grey on stage at the recordBar, Kansas City, 2022
years.h: After the Snow at 40, on The Tonight Show
years.p: The anniversary tour takes Modern English onto Jimmy Fallon's show and NBC's Today.

years.cap: Modern English in a 2022 press photo
years.h: Ten songs from late 2022 become 1 2 3 4
years.p: Grey, Conroy, McDowell and Walker, with Gabriel Sullivan on guitar and Roy Martin on drums.
years.xp: Released on Inkind, the album went back to short songs in the spirit of 1982, Grey told Louder, with a European tour from April 2024.
